verses.1: After these events, there was a vineyard belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite, in Jezreel, right next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.2: Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard, so that I may use it for a garden, since it is so close to my house. In return, I will give you a better vineyard than this, or—if it pleases you—I will give you the value of it in silver."
verses.3: But Naboth replied to Ahab, "Far be it from me to give you the inheritance of my ancestors."
verses.4: Ahab returned to his house, angry and dejected because of what Naboth had said to him, and he refused to eat.
verses.5: His wife Jezebel came to him and asked, "Why is your spirit so dejected that you won't eat bread?"
verses.6: He told her, "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for a garden, and I will give you a better vineyard than it, or the money for it.' But he answered, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
verses.7: Jezebel said to him, "You are now the king of Israel. Get up and eat bread, and let your heart be cheerful. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
verses.8: So Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and the notable men who lived in Naboth's city with him.
verses.9: She wrote in the letters, "Call for a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.10: Place two men, sons of Belial, opposite him, and let them accuse him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him to death."
verses.11: The men of his city, the elders and the notable men who lived in Naboth's city, did as Jezebel had instructed them to do, as written in the letters she had sent them.
verses.12: They called for a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.13: Then the two sons of Belial came in and sat opposite him, and the men of Belial accused Naboth in front of the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed God and the king." They took him outside the city and stoned him to death.
verses.14: Then they sent word to Jezebel, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
verses.15: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which you refused to take for silver, because Naboth is no longer alive—he is dead."
verses.16: When Ahab heard that Naboth had died, he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.17: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
verses.18: "Go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria, for he is now in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.
verses.19: And speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: Did you kill and also take possession? For this, this is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs lap the blood of Naboth, they will also lap your blood—yours, Ahab.'"
verses.20: Ahab said to Elijah, "Have I found you, my enemy?" And he answered, "I have found you because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.21: I will bring calamity upon you and will destroy those who follow you and will cut off from Ahab every one with a crutch and a broken leg in Israel.
verses.22: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the anger you have provoked and the guilt you have caused Israel."
verses.23: And the LORD spoke concerning Jezebel, saying, "The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel.
verses.24: Those who die in the city will be devoured by the dogs, and those who die in the fields will be eaten by the birds of the sky."
verses.25: Yet there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the LORD, incited by Jezebel his wife.
verses.26: He did what was deeply detestable, going after the idols as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the Israelites.
verses.27: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on a sackcloth over his skin, and fasted, walking in sackcloth and going about slowly.
verses.28: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
verses.29: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the calamity in his day, but in the days of his son I will bring it upon his house."

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "sons of Belial" is a fixed expression referring to wicked or lawless men.
- v. 25: "deeply detestable" reflects the Hebrew "lo badad" (literally, "a very bad thing").
- v. 27: "walking in sackcloth and going about slowly" captures the sense of "va-yehalekh at," indicating a slow, penitent walk.
raw:
[1] After these events, there was a vineyard belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite, in Jezreel, right next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

[2] Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard, so that I may use it for a garden, since it is so close to my house. In return, I will give you a better vineyard than this, or—if it pleases you—I will give you the value of it in silver."

[3] But Naboth replied to Ahab, "Far be it from me to give you the inheritance of my ancestors."

[4] Ahab returned to his house, angry and dejected because of what Naboth had said to him, and he refused to eat. 

[5] His wife Jezebel came to him and asked, "Why is your spirit so dejected that you won't eat bread?"

[6] He told her, "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for a garden, and I will give you a better vineyard than it, or the money for it.' But he answered, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

[7] Jezebel said to him, "You are now the king of Israel. Get up and eat bread, and let your heart be cheerful. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

[8] So Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and the notable men who lived in Naboth's city with him.

[9] She wrote in the letters, "Call for a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.

[10] Place two men, sons of Belial, opposite him, and let them accuse him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him to death."

[11] The men of his city, the elders and the notable men who lived in Naboth's city, did as Jezebel had instructed them to do, as written in the letters she had sent them.

[12] They called for a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

[13] Then the two sons of Belial came in and sat opposite him, and the men of Belial accused Naboth in front of the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed God and the king." They took him outside the city and stoned him to death.

[14] Then they sent word to Jezebel, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."

[15] When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which you refused to take for silver, because Naboth is no longer alive—he is dead."

[16] When Ahab heard that Naboth had died, he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

[17] Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:

[18] "Go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria, for he is now in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

[19] And speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: Did you kill and also take possession? For this, this is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs lap the blood of Naboth, they will also lap your blood—yours, Ahab.'"

[20] Ahab said to Elijah, "Have I found you, my enemy?" And he answered, "I have found you because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.

[21] I will bring calamity upon you and will destroy those who follow you and will cut off from Ahab every one with a crutch and a broken leg in Israel.

[22] I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the anger you have provoked and the guilt you have caused Israel."

[23] And the LORD spoke concerning Jezebel, saying, "The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel.

[24] Those who die in the city will be devoured by the dogs, and those who die in the fields will be eaten by the birds of the sky."

[25] Yet there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the LORD, incited by Jezebel his wife.

[26] He did what was deeply detestable, going after the idols as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the Israelites.

[27] When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on a sackcloth over his skin, and fasted, walking in sackcloth and going about slowly.

[28] Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:

[29] "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the calamity in his day, but in the days of his son I will bring it upon his house."

---
Notes
- v. 10: "sons of Belial" is a fixed expression referring to wicked or lawless men.
- v. 25: "deeply detestable" reflects the Hebrew "lo badad" (literally, "a very bad thing").
- v. 27: "walking in sackcloth and going about slowly" captures the sense of "va-yehalekh at," indicating a slow, penitent walk.
